_README: G13 FAMILY-LAW CORPUS GAP MANIFEST - SEED / PLANNING DOCUMENT. NOT INGESTIBLE CORPUS.
This records WHICH provisions the 5 family-law benchmark questions require and
where each must be sourced. It contains NO statute text on purpose.
Fabricated statute text in a legal retrieval system is worse than missing statute
text: a wrong section quoted with confidence is a professional-harm event.
VERIFIED 2026-05-10 by the CORPUS/RETRIEVAL agent (independent recount):
Transfer of Property 344, NI Act 252, Indian Contract 188, Specific Relief 44.
ZERO chunks for: CrPC, PWDVA 2005, HMA 1955, Hindu Minority & Guardianship 1956,
'Hindu Marriage Act' appears ONCE, as scraped website NAVIGATION MENU text filed
under act 'Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023' (corpus index 357) - not statute text.
'498A' appears ONCE, as a cross-reference INSIDE the BNS s.87 chunk.
Production BM25 index holds the SAME 3972 docs, so it agrees with free_corpus.
BM25 RANKING IS HEALTHY: 3/3 control probes returned the correct act 5/5 in top-5.
The failure is CORPUS COVERAGE, not retrieval quality.

sections.description: Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents. The Magistrate may order payment of a monthly allowance for a wife unable to maintain herself, and for children and parents.
Procedure for claiming maintenance - application by the person entitled to it, inquiry, and proof of marital status.
Arrest and detention in default of payment of maintenance; enforcement of maintenance orders.

required_provisions.act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

sections.description: Definitions - 'domestic violence' (physical, sexual, verbal, emotional or economic abuse; harassment; harm or threats) and the protected persons.
Duties of police officers - to inform the aggrieved person of her rights, to provide protection measures, and to arrange medical examination.

required_provisions.act: Indian Penal Code, 1860 (repealed -> Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023)

sections.note: Cited in gold answers for entrustment of property/dowry. BNS s.316 is the successor.

sections.description: Husband or relative of the husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.
sections.note: Repealed, replaced by BNS s.85. Corpus holds only a cross-reference inside the BNS s.87 chunk, not a retrievable provision.

sections.description: Divorce - grounds including adultery, cruelty, desertion, conversion, and (post-2017) mental illness or virulent and malignant form of leprosy.

Divorce by mutual consent. Sub-s.(1A), inserted w.e.f. 2019, allows a fresh divorce petition after one year with no resumption of cohabitation following an RCR decree. Sub-s.(2) covers irretrievable breakdown and the two-year / agreed-separation route.
Guardian of a minor - natural guardian / court-appointed guardian framework; relevant to child custody (hfl_04).
Guardian's duty to ward - duty to look after the minor, to provide for education, and to take all steps necessary for the minor's care, maintenance and protection.
sections.note: VERIFY the gold answer's intent for hfl_02 before ingesting - it cites s.25 in a maintenance context.

ingestion_notes.expected_input: Per-act JSON, one file per statute, under DATA/Statutes/json/
ingestion_notes.runtime_loader: kaanoon_test/system_adapters/vectorless_bm25_store.py reads kaanoon_test/free_corpus/statute_chunks.json at startup (line ~309), so a regenerated free_corpus file is picked up with no code change.
steps: 1. Obtain VERBATIM bare-act text for HMA 1955, PWDVA 2005, CrPC 1973 and HMG Act 1956 from an authoritative source (India Code / legislative.gov.in) - NOT from memory.
2. Save as DATA/Statutes/json/Hindu_Marriage_Act_1955.json etc., one act per file.
3. Run StatuteSectionChunker over those files to emit schema-shaped chunks.
5. Rebuild PERMANENT_RAG_FILES/STATUTE_DATABASE/legal_db_statutes_prod_bm25.pkl and legal_db_statutes_bm25.pkl from the new corpus.
6. Re-run pytest kaanoon_test/test_g13_family_law_retrieval.py - it must go green.
ingestion_notes.NOTE_ON_REALITY: Steps 1-2 are BLOCKED on obtaining authoritative text. Nothing in this repo is a family-law bare act: kaanoon_test/indian_kanoon_collection.json holds 196 court JUDGMENTS that merely CITE HMA/PWDVA, and the 39 chunked acts are commercial/criminal. A human must supply authoritative text. This agent deliberately wrote none.

secondary_defects_found.title: 3371 of 3972 chunks (85%) have a MALFORMED section_number
secondary_defects_found.detail: Values are subsection markers - '(a)' 345x, '(b)' 345x, '(2)' 287x, '(1)' 278x, '(3)' 200x - not real section numbers. Example: act 'Negotiable Instruments Act 1881', section_number '1.'. Any consumer trusting section_number metadata (citation grounding, provenance, per-section dedup) will mis-behave.

secondary_defects_found.title: Mega-chunks pollute every retrieved context
secondary_defects_found.detail: 5 chunks exceed 276,000 chars against a 482-char median. 'Consumer Protection Act 2019 s.2 of 1974' is 824,171 chars of state-amendment footnotes quoting bare numbers like 'Section 125', 'Section 406', 'Section 13', 'Section 9'. BM25 surfaces it for nearly every query.

secondary_defects_found.title: The measured context_section_recall is almost entirely NUMERIC COINCIDENCE
secondary_defects_found.detail: rag_benchmark/metrics.py::sections_in() matches any '(section|sec.) <digits>' string in raw text, so the CPA mega-chunk manufactures gold hits. Measured against act-correct provenance: top-5 = 0 REAL / 3 mentions, top-10 = 0 REAL / 6, top-20 = 1 REAL / 20 (real share 0.05). The true context_section_recall is therefore ~0.00, not the reported 0.20; the 0.42-0.82 seen at deeper K is an artefact.
